title: $\alpha_f$ is a morphism of ring objects
statement:
Give $f^*\Lambda_Y$ the ring object structure transported along the strong
monoidal functor $f^*$ ([def-sfb-finite-upper-star-monoidal]). Then
$\alpha_f\colon f^*\Lambda_Y\to\Lambda_X$ ([def-sfb-alpha]) is a morphism of
ring objects.

proof.text:
Write $P=p_Y^*$, $H=f^*$, $F=H\circ P$, and $G=p_X^*$. Write $(\Lambda,m,u)$ for the coefficient ring object. By [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients] the ring on $P\Lambda$ is the transport along $P$, and the ring on $G\Lambda$ is the transport along $G$. Use the strong monoidal structure on $H$ of [def-sfb-finite-upper-star-monoidal]. In the notation of [det-def-sfb-ring-object-transport], the lax comparison maps of the composite are $c^F_{A,B}=H(c^P_{A,B})\circ c^H_{PA,PB}$ and $e^F=H(e^P)\circ e^H$. Thus the multiplication obtained by transporting first along $P$ and then along $H$ is
$$H(Pm\circ c^P_{\Lambda,\Lambda})\circ c^H_{P\Lambda,P\Lambda}=F(m)\circ c^F_{\Lambda,\Lambda},$$
and its unit is $H(Pu\circ e^P)\circ e^H=F(u)\circ e^F$, by preservation of composition. These are exactly the direct transport formulas. Consequently the specified ring structures on $f^*\Lambda_Y$ and $\Lambda_X$ are the transported structures on $F\Lambda$ and $G\Lambda$.

proof.text: Let $\tau:F\Rightarrow G$ be the underlying natural transformation of [def-sfb-pullback-from-point-comp-iso]. By [def-sfb-alpha], $\alpha_f=\tau_\Lambda$. The statement of [lem-sfb-pullback-from-point-comp-monoidal] says that this very comparison is monoidal for the strong monoidal structures on $F$ and $G$. Thus it satisfies the unit and tensor compatibility needed to apply the monoidal-transformation assertion of the transport lemma, with domain the category of condensed abelian groups and codomain the category of abelian pro-étale sheaves on $X$.

source.place: Last sentence: monoidality of the comparison

proof.text:
Apply clause 3 of [det-def-sfb-ring-object-transport] to the monoidal transformation $\tau:F\Rightarrow G$ at the ring object $\Lambda$. It gives that $\tau_\Lambda$ preserves multiplication and unit for the transported rings identified in step 1. Explicitly the multiplication identity is
$$\tau_\Lambda\circ F(m)\circ c^F_{\Lambda,\Lambda}=G(m)\circ\tau_{\Lambda\otimes\Lambda}\circ c^F_{\Lambda,\Lambda}=G(m)\circ c^G_{\Lambda,\Lambda}\circ(\tau_\Lambda\otimes\tau_\Lambda),$$
and the unit identity is $\tau_\Lambda\circ F(u)\circ e^F=G(u)\circ\tau_{\mathbf1}\circ e^F=G(u)\circ e^G$. The first equality in each chain is naturality; the second is monoidality. By the definition of a morphism of ring objects in [det-def-sfb-ring-object-monoid], these identities say exactly that $\alpha_f=\tau_\Lambda:f^*\Lambda_Y\to\Lambda_X$ is a morphism of ring objects.
